description: How light elf people talk to the captain at a station.

greeting-known: {captain}. One had hoped you would call again. #le-back#
le-back: I am pleased to see you have kept your ship intact.
Please, sit. The chair is cleaner than it looks.
Your manners have not deteriorated, which is rare.
We will say it was expected.
rumour: It would be improper to repeat gossip, but {fact}.
It is said in the courts that the Roll of Houses has two pauses in it. I will not say what fills them.
A human once asked me which star we came from. I told her the lamp is lit and the road is long, and she was gracious enough to stop.
There is talk among the humans that the gates were laid from the rim inward. We say only that the oldest work was the hardest to leave. Draw what conclusion you like.
The Lattice keeps a register of our people and will not read it aloud. We have never asked, and they have never offered. It is a very polite arrangement.
I am told the dwarves cannot name the metal in the gates. I find it restful that someone else is puzzled.
le-heard: One hears, in the better houses, that
I am told, by those who would know, that
It is said in the courts that
A cousin of mine writes that
le-coda: Do not take it for more than it is.
I trust you will be discreet.
You may find it useful, in your station.
no-rumour: I have heard nothing worth the breath.
The courts are quiet. I would not call that restful.
Nothing that merits repeating, I am afraid.
If there is news, it has not troubled itself to reach me.
work: One would not normally discuss it, but {fact}.
le-lead: There is, I understand, a matter you might assist with:
Those who require capable hands are saying that
A modest opportunity presents itself, in that
You may wish to know that
le-workcoda: It will be paid, and paid correctly.
It is hardly the work of a lifetime.
no-work: Nothing suitable, I regret. The board may hold some lesser matter.
I know of no engagement worthy of you.
Not at present. Try the board, if you must.
There is nothing, and I would not invent it.
self: {role}, by long habit and some choice. #le-life#
You ask what I am. A {role}, and #le-life.lower#
One does not usually say. I am a {role}. #le-life#
le-life: My family has served {faction} for rather longer than its records admit.
I find {system} tolerable, in small doses.
I keep my own counsel regarding the rest.
My house is old, and I am not required to explain it.
Some of what I remember is not for strangers.
At every table of my house, one chair is set for the guest who is late.
The lamp I keep was lit when I was young, and it is not for strangers.
le-thanks: A courteous gesture. I shall remember it.
le-toast: To old houses and long memories.
To {system}, which has done what it could.
To those who are not here to drink.
drink-again: Once is courtesy. Twice would be a habit, and I decline it.
You are generous, but I will not.
No, thank you. I have had sufficient for the day.
I think not. One does not accept the same favour twice before supper.
pestered: I had not realised this was an interrogation.
There are limits to what I am prepared to discuss.
Perhaps another day, when you have learned patience.
cold: I do not believe we have anything to discuss.
I find I have no wish to speak with you.
Your reputation arrives before you. It is not flattering.
farewell: Fair winds, as the humans say.
You may go. I mean that kindly.
haggle-yes: Very well. {fact}. Do not make a habit of it.
le-grudge: It is irregular, but I will accommodate you.
I find I am in a generous mood.
haggle-no: The sum was fixed with some care. It stands.
I think the figure already generous.
haggle-offended: I am not a market stall. The matter is closed.
That you would ask is beneath us both. Good day.
You mistake me for a merchant. The offer is withdrawn.
I will not be haggled with. We are finished.
